_meta.indication: ULORIC is a xanthine oxidase (XO) inhibitor indicated for the chronic management of hyperuricemia in patients with gout.
_meta.receipt_date: July 17, 2008 (complete response to the August 2, 2006 action letter).

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents.
pivotal_trials.design: Six-month, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trial comparing Uloric 40 mg and 80 mg to allopurinol 300 mg (200 mg in renal impairment); randomization stratified by renal function.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects with a serum uric acid of less than 6 mg/dL at the final study visit.
pivotal_trials.n: N (ITT): febuxostat 40 mg 757; febuxostat 80 mg 756; allopurinol 755.
pivotal_trials.result: Serum urate <6.0 mg/dL at final visit: febuxostat 80 mg 507/756 (67%) vs allopurinol 318/755 (42%), difference 25% (95% CI 20%, 30%), p<0.0001 (superiority); febuxostat 40 mg 342/757 (45%), difference 3% (95% CI -2%, 8%), p=0.233, lower bound above the prespecified -10% non-inferiority margin.

nct_ctgov.title: Efficacy and Safety of Oral Febuxostat in Participants With Gout

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=1% and >=0.5% greater than placebo): liver function abnormalities, nausea, arthralgia, and rash. Liver function abnormalities 6.6% (40 mg) / 4.6% (80 mg) vs 0.7% placebo. Transaminase elevations >3x ULN observed. A higher rate of cardiovascular thromboembolic events was seen with ULORIC [0.74 per 100 P-Y (95% CI 0.36-1.37)] than allopurinol [0.60 per 100 P-Y (95% CI 0.16-1.53)].
target_moa: Febuxostat is a xanthine oxidase inhibitor that achieves its therapeutic effect by decreasing serum uric acid.
modality: Small molecule (oral immediate-release tablet; molecular weight 316.38).

advisory_committee.vote: Arthritis Advisory Committee voted 12 to 0 in favor of approval, with one abstention.

summary.text: Uloric was approved on its third review cycle for the chronic management of hyperuricemia in patients with gout, after two prior approvable letters driven by a cardiovascular safety signal; approval followed a 12-to-0 Arthritis Advisory Committee vote and was conditioned on required postmarketing (505(o)) clinical trials, including a cardiovascular outcomes trial versus allopurinol and a theophylline drug-interaction study.

citations.quote: This new drug application provides for the use of Uloric in the chronic management of hyperuricemia in patients with gout.

This is the third cycle review of Uloric. This novel xanthine oxidase inhibitor received approvable letters on the last two review cycles based predominantly on a signal of cardiovascular toxicity which had not been adequately evaluated to allow for a complete risk-benefit assessment of the available doses of the proposed drug product.

requirement.text: A randomized, controlled trial of adequate size and duration to determine whether the use of Uloric is associated with a moderate increase in the risk of serious adverse cardiovascular outcomes as compared to allopurinol.
